newsitem.title: USA: IBM expands disk drive plant in San Jose.
newsitem.headline: IBM expands disk drive plant in San Jose.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said it is expanding its disk drive manufacturing to turn its San Jose facility into the world's largest disk platter factory, to meet increased demand.

An IBM spokeswoman said the computer giant is adding several manufacturing lines to its current 316,000 square foot facility so that it will increase its production of disk drive platters by the "several more million."
IBM will be doing some "significant hiring" for the plant, but the spokeswoman did not have any specific numbers on how many people IBM will hire, or on future production capacity.
"We are adding several lines," said an IBM spokeswoman. "There will be a significant amount of hiring for this plant."

IBM said the move is part of its ongoing $1.32 billion expansion of its storage business, which it started last March with a $500 million investment in its storage manufacturing capacity. Last month, IBM said it will build a new plant in Mulhuddart, Ireland, outside Dublin, and that storage will be the first IBM tenant at the new facility.
In San Jose, the expanded plant will continue to make platters, which are the key component for hard disk drives. Platters are known as "disk media" which record data.

"Driven by strong PC sales, as well as high-end storage needs such as network computing, the demand for IBM's innovative hard disk drives has increased dramatically worldwide," said Tony Razouk, director of IBM disk manufacturing, in a statement.

IBM said that the San Jose expansion will be completed by mid 1997. IBM is a captive user of its hard disk drives, in its computer systems across the board, from mainframes to PCs and it also sells them to other companies, such as Apple Computer Inc and Dell Computer Corp.
